the OMC32 acrosomal matrix polypeptide binds to the detergent-soluble proteins acrosin, SPACA-3, lactadherrin, and IZU- MO1, and that the binding of OMC32 to acrosin and lactadherrin is disrupted during the LPC-induced AR.

the acrosin-binding OMC32 polypetide interacts with acrosin and other acrosomal protein complexes and that the interaction of the OMC polypeptide with the detergent-soluble protein complex regulates the release of acrosomal hydrolases during the acrosomal reaction.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the release of acrosomal contents during fertilization.
the identification of acrosomal matrix proteins and the elucidation of their role(s) in sperm function.
the identification of a novel acrosomal matrix polypeptide and its role in sperm acrosomal function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

OMC32 is a multifunctional protein complex that interacts with acrosin as well as other sperm proteins and regulates the release of sperm hydrolases and other acrosomal components during the acrosomal reaction.

the interaction of the 32-kDa matrix polypeptide of the bovine sperm outer acrosomal matrix with detergent-solubilized acrosomal proteins (acrosin, lactodherin, SPAC3, and IZZUMO1) is a critical step in the acrosome reactions.
the OMC32 matrix complex may be involved in the regulation of acrosin release during the acrosomal exocytosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OMC32 protein complex is a stable acrosome matrix protein that interacts with acrosin and other acrosomal protein complexes to regulate sperm function.
the acrosin-binding OMC32 polynucleotide (32-kDa) is a major component of the OMCrpf polypeptides and that OMC32 is involved in the regulation of sperm function.
the OMCrpf polypeptide (OMC32) interacts with the acrosomal proteins and is involved in the regulation of sperm acrosome reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OMC32 matrix complex is involved in the release of hydolases during the acrosomal reaction.
the acrosomal matrix is not a static entity, rather, it is a dynamic structure that undergoes a significant reorganization during the acrosomal reaction.
the OMC32 protein may be a potential candidate for sperm selection for assisted reproduction technologies.
